title: Georeferencing with Zooniverse!
content:
Where exactly was a museum specimen collected? A new Zooniverse project invites volunteers to help turn location information from museum records into points on a map, making biodiversity data easier for researchers to use. The project also introduces new mapping tools that will eventually support many different kinds of research on Zooniverse.

Yesterday, we launched a brand-new project: Notes from Nature – Putting Biodiversity on the Map. This project invites volunteers to help georeference museum specimen records by matching locality descriptions to places on a map. Museum specimen labels include locality information to describe the place where a specimen was collected. Georeferencing is the process of converting that locality information into geographic coordinates (e.g. latitude and longitude).

Prior to this project, the Notes from Nature research team would ask volunteers to transcribe specimen records in Zooniverse, then export the locality data to GEOLocate for georeferencing. GEOLocate includes tools for automated georeferencing (based on the transcribed locality information), and the data would then be reviewed and corrected on the GEOLocate platform.

title: A New Space for Experimentation with Zooniverse
content:
Zooniverse is creating a new way for research teams to experiment with tools and approaches that aren’t currently possible within the standard Zooniverse Project Builder. These Custom Front Ends remain connected to Zooniverse infrastructure while giving researchers more flexibility to test new ways for volunteers to take part in research.

Since Galaxy Zoo launched in 2007, the founding of Zooniverse in 2009, and the launch of the Zooniverse DIY Project Builder platform (zooniverse.org/lab) in 2015, Zooniverse has helped hundreds of researchers and millions of volunteers work together to unlock data for research and discovery. The Project Builder provides a shared set of tools that enable research teams to create projects for a broad range of volunteers, data and task types. Every project undergoes extensive testing and review by both the Zooniverse team and our volunteer beta community to help ensure a high-quality experience across supported browsers and devices. We remain committed to supporting and advancing the Zooniverse platform, which is the foundation of Zooniverse and will continue to power the vast majority of projects in the years ahead.
